# FAQ — recurring pitfalls and their solutions

### PHPUnit test failures with FFI loading errors

<!-- id=FAQ-001, date=2026-04-01, tags=phpunit ports ffi, trigger=test failures with "Failed loading .so" or "Address already in use", status=active -->

ScanMePHP has an optional C++ FFI encoder (`clib/`). The `QrReferenceTest`
suite compares the FFI encoder against a reference; if the shared library is
not built for the current platform, those tests error out. Build it first:
`cd clib && rm -rf build && cmake -B build -S . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build build -j`.
There is no background daemon in this project, so "Address already in use" is
not a risk here (unlike the workerman-bundle workflow this was adapted from).

### Coverage is not gated in CI

<!-- id=FAQ-002, date=2026-04-01, tags=coverage phpunit, trigger=PR discussion about coverage floor, status=active -->

CI runs `composer test` (PHPUnit) without a coverage floor. Coverage requires
Xdebug or PCOV, which are not in the CI matrix (`coverage: none`). If you want
to verify coverage locally, run `vendor/bin/phpunit --coverage-text` with
Xdebug enabled. Do not add a coverage gate without first deciding the floor
with the maintainer.

### FFI extension is optional but present in CI

<!-- id=FAQ-003, date=2026-04-01, tags=ffi, trigger=questions about whether ext-ffi is required, status=active -->

`ext-ffi` is enabled in CI (`setup-php` with `extensions: ffi, gd`) but is not
in `composer.json` `require` — the project is zero-runtime-dependency. The
native PHP encoder is the fallback when FFI is unavailable. Tests that require
FFI should be marked skipped when the library or extension is missing, not
failed.

### PHPStan reports `*NEVER*` or undefined `FFI\CData` property

<!-- id=FAQ-005, date=2026-04-01, tags=phpstan ffi baseline, trigger=PHPStan reports *NEVER* range errors or undefined FFI\CData property/method, status=active -->

PHPStan's range reasoning does not model QR matrix dimensions, so comparisons
in `FastEncoder` and `MaskSelector` (e.g. `>=` against a value PHPStan infers
as `*NEVER*`) produce `identical.alwaysFalse` / `greaterOrEqual.invalid` /
`booleanAnd.alwaysFalse`. These are false positives and live in
`phpstan-baseline.neon` — do not add `@phpstan-ignore` comments or widen types
to silence them; fix the source if it is a real bug, otherwise accept the
baseline entry. Separately, `FfiEncoder` accesses dynamic C struct properties
and C functions via `FFI::cdef`, which PHPStan cannot resolve — it is excluded
from analysis (see `decisions.md` DEC-005 and issue #41 for the refactor that
would bring it back). Excluding files has a cost: it hid the bugs in #39, so
prefer the refactor over a permanent exclusion.

### Zero runtime dependencies principle

<!-- id=FAQ-004, date=2026-04-01, tags=zero-deps, trigger=proposing to add a runtime dependency, status=active -->

ScanMePHP has **no external runtime dependencies** (`require` lists only
`php` and `composer-plugin-api`). PHPUnit, Paratest, ext-gd, PHPStan,
php-cs-fixer, rector and `composer/composer` (for plugin stubs) are dev/test
only and never ship. Never add anything to `require` — propose it first and
get maintainer approval.

### Native encoder extension name is `scanmeqr` (no underscore)

<!-- id=FAQ-006, date=2026-04-01, tags=ffi phpunit zero-deps, trigger=adding a new extension_loaded('scanmeqr') call site or touching encoder selection, status=active -->

The C extension registers its module as `"scanmeqr"` (no underscore) — source
of truth: `php-ext/scanme_qr.c:33` `zend_module_entry`. `QRCode::createDefaultEncoder()`
gates on `extension_loaded('scanmeqr')` together with `class_exists(NativeEncoder)`.
Note `class_exists('CrazyGoat\ScanMePHP\NativeEncoder')` is **true even without
the extension** because `src/NativeEncoder.php` is a conditional `if/else` class
declaration whose `else` branch still defines the class — so `extension_loaded`
is the real guard and `class_exists` is not sufficient on its own. Issue #39 was
this exact typo (`scanme_qr` vs `scanmeqr`) and was invisible to behavior tests
because no CI machine has the extension compiled. The regression guard is a
source-string contract test, `tests/ExtensionNameConsistencyTest::testAllEncoderSelectionPathsUseTheSameExtensionName`,
which pins `src/QRCode.php`, `src/NativeEncoder.php`, and `src/Composer/Plugin.php`.
**When adding a new `extension_loaded('scanmeqr')` call site, add the file to
that test's `$files` array.** (The C-side `php-ext/scanme_qr.c` literal is not
yet pinned — see the follow-up issue for that gap.)
